body.statement:
Use \(L_N(H)\) and \(\delta_\star\) from \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\).  Fix \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\).  Let \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) be any deterministic map from arm-outcome tables to sets of complete weak orders such that, for every fixed binary schedule satisfying the design and stratified-interference assumptions,
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in
       \mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
If \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\) for every compatible \(H\), then in fact
\[
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H)=\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
 \qquad\text{for every compatible }H.
\]
More sharply, if \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\) and \(\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\), there is a deterministic schedule realizing \(N\) for which the noncoverage probability is at least
\[
 L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star>\alpha.
\]
Thus no family indexed by all \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) can both preserve uniform coverage at every level and be a strict contained refinement at some compatible table at every level.  This obstruction does not assert impossibility of a consonant strict refinement for \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\).
body.proof_tex:
Theorem \(\texttt{thm:deterministic-order-atom-frontier}\) proves
\[
 0<\delta_\star\le\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}.
\]
Thus the present hypothesis \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\) implies \(\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\). For every compatible \(H\), that theorem gives
\[
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
 =\mathfrak O_H
 =\{\mathcal O(N):N\in\mathcal N(H)\}
\]
and shows that every uniformly valid deterministic table-measurable rule \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) contains \(\mathfrak O_H\). Under the assumed containment \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\), both inclusions therefore hold and
\[
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H)=\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
\]
for every compatible \(H\).

For the sharper schedule witness, fix \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\) and suppose \(\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\). The realizability construction in Lemma \(\texttt{lem:deterministic-coverage-iff}\) supplies a deterministic binary schedule in the stated class with \(N^\star=N\). For that schedule, the exact identity in the same lemma gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
 \mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\\
 &\quad=
 \sum_{\substack{H':(H',N)\in\mathfrak J}}
 L_N(H')\,
 \mathbf 1\!\left\{\mathcal O(N)\notin
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H')\right\}\\
 &\quad\ge L_N(H)
 \ge\delta_\star
 >\alpha,
\end{aligned}
\]
where nonnegativity gives the first inequality and Lemma \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\) gives the second. This proves the claimed witness and contradicts uniform coverage whenever an order is omitted.

Finally, suppose a family indexed by all \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) were uniformly valid, contained in the baseline at every compatible table, and strictly contained at some compatible table at every level. Choosing any \(\alpha\in(0,\delta_\star)\) contradicts the equality just proved. Theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-weak-order-coverage}\) confirms that the baseline itself is uniformly valid. The separate order-atom frontier theorem sharpens the forced-equality range to \(0<\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) and deliberately leaves deterministic consonant refinement at \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), as well as randomized reporting, unresolved.
body.justification: The theorem is the low-threshold corollary of the exact deterministic coverage characterization and the stronger order-specific atom frontier.
body.gap: Deterministic consonant strict refinement remains open for \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), and randomized reporting is outside the characterization.
body.consumer: Software designers can avoid closure searches below the computable order-atom threshold and focus on the unresolved boundary and upper-level regime.
